subject: ITU-Y3172
claim: ITU-T Y.3172 provides an architectural framework for machine learning in future networks including IMT-2020.

subject: AI-Readiness
claim: ITU AI readiness work treats data availability/quality as a readiness dimension.

subject: AI-Readiness
claim: ITU AI readiness work identifies standards as important to trust, interoperability and compliance.

subject: Radio-Regulations
claim: ITU Radio Regulations provide the international framework for radio-frequency spectrum use and interference protection.

subject: Coexistence-Studies
claim: ITU-R coexistence work provides precedent for interference calculation/simulation and mitigation evaluation.

subject: Aeronautical-Propagation
claim: ITU-R P.528 is a relevant propagation recommendation for aeronautical mobile/radionavigation analysis.

subject: IMT-2020-mobile-station
claim: ITU-R M.2175 addresses unwanted-emission characteristics of IMT-2020 mobile stations.

subject: 5GS
claim: 3GPP TS 23.501 is the system architecture specification for the 5G System.

subject: 5GS
claim: 3GPP TS 23.502 specifies procedures for the 5G System.

subject: 5G-management
claim: TS 28.530 covers management and orchestration concepts, use cases and requirements.

subject: 5G-management
claim: TS 28.532 covers generic management services.

subject: 5G-management
claim: TS 28.533 covers the management/orchestration architecture framework.

subject: 5G-network-resources
claim: TS 28.540 specifies the 5G Network Resource Model Stage 1.

subject: 5G-network-resources
claim: TS 28.541 covers Stage 2/3 aspects of the 5G Network Resource Model.

subject: ICAO-Annex-10-Vol-V
claim: ICAO Annex 10 Volume V covers aeronautical radio-frequency spectrum utilization; current ICAO listing shows Amendment 91 dated 2025.
review_note: REVIEW: sources.csv URL points to Amendment 90 (12-7-22) while claim says Amendment 91; verify edition

subject: Radio-Altimeter
claim: ICAO 5G guidance identifies 4.2–4.4 GHz as the radio-altimeter operating band.

subject: Radio-Altimeter
claim: ICAO guidance identifies radio-altimeter information as supporting safety-related aircraft functions.

subject: 5G-C-band
claim: ICAO guidance addresses potential harmful interference to radio altimeters from cellular 5G deployments in adjacent bands.

subject: Protection-analysis
claim: ICAO coexistence guidance identifies base-station characteristics and aircraft geometry/height as relevant to protection analysis.

subject: Protection-analysis
claim: ICAO guidance recommends an air-to-ground propagation model for protection-area analysis.

subject: Mitigation
claim: ICAO guidance identifies maximum 5G power limits and downward antenna tilting among mitigation measures.

subject: Airport-protection
claim: ICAO guidance identifies 5G prohibition/precautionary zones around airports as a possible mitigation.

subject: Aviation-5G-coexistence
claim: ICAO guidance recommends consultation with aviation safety regulators, experts and airspace users.

subject: FAA-5G-program
claim: FAA describes aviation/wireless coordination and sharing of 5G transmitter location/power information.

subject: FAA-5G-program
claim: FAA describes airport-specific mitigation including buffer zones and transmitter adjustments.

subject: FAA-2026-rule
claim: FAA's 2026 final-rule material establishes minimum radio-altimeter performance requirements for neighboring-band wireless interference.
review_note: V2: superseded in detail by CLM-101..CLM-120

subject: FAA-FCC
claim: FAA states its 2026 altimeter rule was coordinated with FCC spectrum action.

subject: FAA-AC-20-199
claim: AC 20-199 provides installation and testing guidance including external RF-interference tolerance.

subject: CEPT-ECC362
claim: ECC Report 362 studies coexistence involving mobile/fixed communications and radio altimeters.

subject: India-NFAP-2025
claim: NFAP-2025 is India's national frequency allocation framework and supports next-generation wireless technologies including 5G Advanced/IMT-2030.

subject: India-NFAP-2025
claim: NFAP-2025 identifies the 2024 ITU Radio Regulations as a foundational international spectrum reference.

subject: Indian-WPC
claim: DoT identifies WPC Wing as responsible for frequency assignments for terrestrial networks.

subject: Indian-WPC
claim: DoT work allocation assigns spectrum planning, management and regulation functions to WPC.

subject: Indian-WPC
claim: WPC's mandate includes international/regional radiocommunication coordination on behalf of India.

subject: Telecommunications-Act-2023
claim: The Telecommunications Act 2023 includes a condition that secondary spectrum assignment must not cause harmful interference to the primary assignee.

subject: India-AIC-19-2025
claim: India AIC 19/2025 defines radio-altimeter-tolerant aircraft in relation to 5G C-band emissions.
review_note: INCOMPLETE: omits effective date 2027-12-31; see CLM-131

subject: India-AIC-19-2025
claim: India AIC 19/2025 specifies operational limitations for non-radio-altimeter-tolerant aircraft in Indian airspace.
review_note: INCOMPLETE: limitations not in force until 2027-12-31; see CLM-131..133

subject: India-DoT
claim: DoT maintains an official repository of current telecom Acts and Rules.

subject: TSDSI
claim: TSDSI provides an Indian standards/transposition path for 3GPP activity.

subject: Cross-domain-coordination
claim: The evidence base supports treating cross-domain aviation/telecom coordination and data sharing as a core coexistence mechanism.

subject: Dynamic-agent-action
claim: Because India, US and European approaches evolve independently, policy retrieval should be jurisdiction- and version-aware rather than using one universal rule.

subject: Safety-margin-score
claim: A simulator's numeric safety-margin score should be labelled simulation/model output unless directly tied to an authoritative regulatory threshold.

subject: FAA-rule
claim: FAA's final rule (Docket FAA-2025-5666) requires radio altimeters on Part 91 aircraft operating in the 48 contiguous states and DC to meet minimum performance needed to withstand interference from wireless services licensed across 3.7-4.2 GHz.

subject: FAA-rule
claim: Compliance dates: Part 121 operators and large Part 129 aircraft (30+ seats or payload over 7,500 lb) by 2030-12-30; all other Part 91-bound aircraft (incl. parts 125, 133, 135, 136, 137, 194 and remaining Part 129) by 2034-10-31.

subject: FAA
claim: FAA states it regulates the aircraft and its operation, not the interference environment; the interference-tolerance mask specifies aircraft tolerance and is not a published limit on wireless emissions.

subject: ITM
claim: The interference tolerance mask (ITM) at or below 500 ft AGL defines the maximum RFI the RA system must tolerate at the antenna surface, including a safety margin; final rule added a 4170-4180 MHz entry to Table 1 of 14 CFR 91.220 (the range lies above the FCC-authorized wireless band).

subject: FAA-rule
claim: FAA adopted no ITM requirement above 500 ft AGL, reasoning that FCC caps base-station height at 450 ft AGL so interference at higher altitude is lower owing to added free-space path loss.

subject: safety-margin
claim: FAA's safety analysis applies a 6 dB safety margin above the expected interference environment, citing ICAO Doc 9718 guidance of 6-10 dB for aeronautical safety systems.

subject: MSD
claim: FAA's methodology requires the RA to function reliably at a 35 ft minimum separation distance (sphere centred on base-station antenna phase centre) from any wireless base station when the aircraft is at or below 500 ft AGL; FAA retained 35 ft over industry requests for 300 ft horizontal.

subject: aggregation-factor
claim: For out-of-band emissions into the RA band FAA adopted a 5 dB aggregation factor (reduced from 6 dB in the NPRM), because sites with three co-located transmitters exist.

subject: compatibility-analysis
claim: FAA compatibility table: adjacent-band base-station EIRP 65 dBm/MHz (dual-pol; 62 per polarization) gives 0.4 dBW/m2/MHz at 35 ft; adding 6 dB margin gives 6.4 versus ITM 9.5 dBW/m2/MHz. In-band spurious -28.4 dBm/MHz EIRP (-31.4 per pol) gives -93 dBW/m2/MHz; adding 6 dB margin and 5 dB aggregation gives -82, equal to ITM -82 dBW/m2/MHz.

subject: spurious-limit
claim: FCC allows an alternative conducted spurious limit of -46 dBm/MHz instead of -28.4 dBm/MHz EIRP; this corresponds to up to 17.6 dBi antenna gain in the RA band.

subject: FCC-R&O
claim: FCC's July 2026 Upper C-band Report and Order (as described by FAA) makes 3980-4140 MHz available for terrestrial wireless with a 4140-4160 MHz guard band and 4160-4200 MHz repacked for fixed-satellite service; CONUS and DC only; earliest new service 2030-12-31; auction must finish by 2027-07-04.

subject: FCC-R&O
claim: FCC Upper C-band technical limits relevant to RAs: base-station EIRP up to 65 dBm/MHz, transmitter height up to 450 ft AGL, out-of-band emission into the RA band no more than -28.4 dBm/MHz dual-polarization EIRP or -46 dBm/MHz conducted.

subject: FCC-R&O
claim: FCC's order also tightens Lower C-band (3.7-3.98 GHz) emissions into the RA band from the 2020 limit of -13 dBm/MHz conducted to the new -28.4 dBm/MHz EIRP or -46 dBm/MHz conducted.

subject: FCC-R&O
claim: FCC's order creates a radio-altimeter retrofit rebate program funded by Upper C-band auction winners, expected within 6-12 months after the auction; foreign operators are not eligible.

subject: wireless-carriers
claim: Lower C-band licensees made voluntary (not statutory) commitments to coordinate power and limit emissions into the RA band until 2028-01-01; AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon said they are prepared to extend until the FCC's earliest Upper C-band access date, and 14 further licensees had filed extensions by 2026-07-15.

subject: RA-data
claim: RA data feeds low-visibility approach and landing (autoland, CAT II/III, SA CAT, EFVS), terrain awareness (TAWS), collision avoidance (TCAS), windshear detection and rotorcraft automation; erroneous RA data can go undetected by the pilot.

subject: safety-case
claim: FAA's safety case uses worst-case FCC-compliant base-station configurations; a single critical location (e.g. transmitters under a flight path near an airport) drives risk because safety is not traded off across geographies.

subject: FAA-rule
claim: The FAA rule does not apply to Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico or other US territories, nor to airspace 3-12 nm offshore; the FCC order authorizes Upper C-band base stations only in the contiguous US and DC.

subject: RTCA-EUROCAE-MOPS
claim: The joint RTCA SC-239 / EUROCAE WG-119 radio-altimeter MOPS is scheduled for publication in March 2027 (validation scheduled September 2026); FAA did not adopt it as a requirement, and EASA asked FAA to wait for it.

subject: MSD-dispute
claim: Industry commenters (CTIA) argued for larger separation (300 ft horizontal, 50 ft vertical) while others (Lockheed Martin) argued 35 ft was too small; FAA kept 35 ft, noting the Lower C-band analysis protected a 25 ft vertical MSD.

subject: AD-2023-10-02
claim: Under FAA AD 2023-10-02, a 'radio altimeter tolerant airplane' must demonstrate tolerance to fundamental 3.7-3.98 GHz emissions and to spurious 4.2-4.4 GHz emissions at or above PSD thresholds in the AD's Figures 1 and 2; non-tolerant airplanes face flight-manual limitations.

subject: FAA-ADs
claim: FAA ADs prohibit certain RA-dependent operations (e.g. low-visibility approaches) at airports and areas identified by NOTAM as affected by 5G C-band interference.

subject: DGCA-order
claim: AIC 19/2025 Appendix A (DGCA order for airplanes) states radio altimeters cannot be relied on if exposed to wireless broadband in 3.3-3.67 GHz (5G C-band in India); undetected anomalies near the ground (e.g. landing flare) could cause loss of continued safe flight and landing.

subject: DGCA-order
claim: The AIC 19/2025 orders apply to all airplanes and all rotorcraft equipped with radio altimeters and state an effective date of 2027-12-31.

subject: DGCA-order
claim: From its effective date, non-RA-tolerant airplanes in Indian airspace are prohibited from: ILS approaches, SA CAT I/II and CAT II/III operations; automatic landing; manual flight-control guidance/HUD to touchdown; and EFVS to touchdown.

subject: DGCA-order
claim: From its effective date, non-RA-tolerant rotorcraft in Indian airspace are prohibited from RA-minimum offshore approaches (barometric minimums required), RA-dependent hover and SAR autopilot modes, and takeoff/landing procedures (Cat A/B or performance class) that need RA data.

subject: DGCA-order
claim: An RA-tolerant aircraft is one whose RA, as installed, demonstrates tolerance to 5G C-band emissions; no action is required for it, and modifying a non-tolerant aircraft to tolerant terminates the limitations. The AIC text sets no numeric tolerance threshold.

subject: DGCA
claim: A trade report describes a DGCA order dated 2025-11-19 requiring airlines to retrofit radio altimeters for tolerance to 3,300-3,670 MHz by 2027-12-31, building on earlier interim restrictions around airports. The primary AIC text frames this as flight-manual limitations on non-tolerant aircraft rather than an explicit retrofit mandate.

subject: COAI-DGCA
claim: Press report: DGCA imposed restrictions on 5G rollout in the 3.3 GHz band near airports over radio-altimeter concerns; operators' body COAI asked for a fixed 18-month phase-out of non-conforming altimeters. India's auctioned C-band is 3300-3670 MHz versus RA band 4200-4400 MHz. Report is undated and gives no distance/power parameters.

subject: separation
claim: India's 5G C-band upper edge (3670 MHz) is 530 MHz below the RA band's lower edge (4200 MHz), a larger separation than the US Lower C-band (3980 MHz upper edge, 220 MHz) - but separation alone does not rule out out-of-band or blocking effects.

subject: RR-5.438
claim: ITU Radio Regulations footnote 5.438 reserves 4200-4400 MHz for aeronautical radionavigation use by radio altimeters on aircraft and associated ground transponders; passive Earth-exploration/space-research sensing may be secondary and gets no altimeter protection.

subject: RR-4.10
locator: RR No. 4.10 (quoted in ICAO MID TDRA presentation)
claim: ITU RR No. 4.10 recognizes that safety aspects of radionavigation and other safety services call for special measures to avoid harmful interference.

subject: M.2059
claim: Rec. ITU-R M.2059 gives technical/operational characteristics and protection criteria for radio altimeters in 4200-4400 MHz for use in compatibility studies; altimeters need about 196 MHz of bandwidth.

subject: NR-bands
claim: 3GPP NR bands: n77 = 3300-4200 MHz, n78 = 3300-3800 MHz, n79 = 4400-5000 MHz; for n77 a note restricts use in the USA to 3450-3550 and 3700-3980 MHz (Canada: 3450-3650 and 3650-3980 MHz).

subject: n77
claim: Because n77 extends to 4200 MHz, equipment capability does not imply authorization: a carrier/configuration in the upper n77 range may sit directly against the RA band, so a network agent must check national authorization before selecting carriers above the licensed range.

subject: ECC-362
claim: ECC Report 362 (approved 2024-11-08) studies radio altimeters in 4200-4400 MHz against public 5G in 3400-3800 MHz and local/private low-medium-power systems in 3800-4200 MHz; only usage-category-1 radio altimeters were considered.

subject: ECC-362
object: 6 dB margin met (BS >1200 m from threshold or >40 m lateral)
claim: For 3400-3800 MHz 5G in the modelled ILS-approach scenario, unwanted-emission studies show margins covering at least the 6 dB ICAO safety margin; the margin is fully covered for base stations more than 1200 m from the runway threshold or 40 m laterally, or with improved out-of-band levels. Measurement campaigns found no interference in tested scenarios and aircraft.

subject: EASA
claim: EASA's assessment says ECC Report 362 does not justify an implementing regulation for fleet-wide radio-altimeter retrofit and favours corrective action on individual aircraft-altimeter combinations where needed; the EU roadmap covers 3.4-4.4 GHz and excludes above 4.4 GHz.

subject: ECC-362
claim: An ICAO regional presentation notes that aviation interests filed comments questioning ECC Report 362's conclusions as not representative of all current altimeters; EUROCONTROL's 2024 study concluded interference cannot be ruled out for all 5G and aircraft conditions.

subject: US-Lower-C-band
claim: US Lower C-band mitigations summarized by ICAO include limits on antenna elevation above the horizon and coordination with FAA for 5G towers near airports, with limits agreed until January 2028.

subject: ICAO
locator: ICAO MID guidance material front matter
claim: ICAO issued State Letter SP 74/1-21/22 (2021-03-25) on safety concerns about broadband cellular near 4.2-4.4 GHz; ICAO MID's RADALT Action Group developed guidance (impact on operations, short-term safeguards, aerodrome methodologies) which FSMP proposed to finalize as an ICAO circular - final publication status not confirmed here.

subject: AD-CF-2025-54
claim: Transport Canada AD CF-2025-54 (2025-11-19) addresses RA interference from 5G C-band across Canadian airspace and reuses the FAA AD 2023-10-02 definitions of radio-altimeter-tolerant aeroplane.

subject: NRSectorCarrier
claim: In 3GPP's network resource model, an NRSectorCarrier object represents the resources of a transmission point tied to one or more cells and carries direction (txDirection), carrier frequencies (arfcnDL/arfcnUL) and channel bandwidths (bSChannelBwDL/UL); the UE is not directly aware of which sector-carrier resources serve it.

subject: NRCellDU
locator: TS 28.541 attribute tables (via SA5 CR drafts)
claim: TS 28.541 defines NRCellDU with administrativeState, operationalState and usageState attributes and an attribute named configuredMaxTxPower; the cell-level or sector-carrier owner of that attribute was not confirmed from the snippet.

subject: TS-28.552
claim: TS 28.552 defines cell load measurements for NRCellDU including PRB usage distributions (histogram of samples), peak DL/UL PRB used (e.g. RRU.MaxPrbUsedDl), average available PRBs (e.g. RRU.PrbAvailUl) and MIMO-aware PRB usage, intended for load monitoring and RRM optimization.

subject: TS-28.552
claim: TS 28.552 also defines PRB usage per SSB beam (RRU.PrbTotUlSSB); 3GPP notes it as input for AI/ML training and management data analytics such as load balancing and reshaping cell coverage.

subject: KB-coverage
claim: The KB contains evidence for load KPIs (PRB usage per cell and per beam) and for the existence of a configurable maximum transmit power attribute, but none on antenna tilt, beam-shape or per-beam power management objects or on their actuation latency; Optimization agent actions of those kinds are unsupported by KB evidence.
